$comment: Scoring rules for a news source. Consumed by the lab script and by the Java job alike: every rule is a named measurement with a weight, so a source score is a plain weighted sum in [0, 100].
niche: practical web development: JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS, HTML, browsers, frameworks, performance, accessibility, SEO, WordPress

rules.measure: share of articles fetched without blocked / paywall / empty-without-js / robots-disallowed / fetch-failed
share of articles where state.publishedAt is present
median age of the articles in days, by state.publishedAt
rules.scoring: full at <= 7 days, zero at >= 60 days, linear between

rules.measure: median state.tokens of the article body
rules.scoring: full inside the band, zero below 200 or above 20000, linear between

rules.measure: median count of headings + code blocks in the markdown
rules.scoring: full at >= 6, zero at 0, linear between

rules.measure: mean jev_rerank score of the articles against the niche
share of articles jev_classify puts in tutorial / news / analysis rather than sponsored / listicle / digest

classes.description: Teaches how to do one thing, with steps and code. Belongs: guides, how-tos, deep dives with code. Does not belong: a list of ten tools.
Reports a concrete event: a release, a browser feature shipping, a standard change, an acquisition. Has a date and a subject.
Argues a position or explains a trend with evidence. Opinion pieces, retrospectives, case studies.
A list of tools, resources, links or tips with a sentence each and no depth. 'Top 10 …', 'Best … in 2026'.
A roundup of links to other articles: newsletter issue, weekly links, 'what happened this week'.
Promotes a product or service the author sells or is paid for, even when framed as a guide.
